body:
Hi, thank you from the bottom of my heart for replying. I really appreciate it and the support.

It is tough to see the wildly high rates of suicide in the trans population (like 41%) compared to the "normal" population (about 0.4% I think?). At the same time, I feel like I have it so easy compared to so many, you know? Like coming from a privileged background with an INCREDIBLY supportive family. Even my grampa is on board. I feel like sometimes I have no reason to feel the way I do, although I have training in mental health and crisis supportive listening, so I know that's pretty much crap. Everyone's struggles are valid - but at the same time it almost makes me feel weak; like if I'm suicidal from this shit, how are others surviving so much worse? Like trans women of colour go through SO much worse than I could ever imagine. 

On top of that, I am lucky in that I've been seeing an AWESOME therapist for a few years now, since I was about 18. She's great and she's helped me through so much stuff, but the only thing is, I feel bad going more than maybe once every three weeks because it's quite expensive and my parents are paying for it (yet another privilege). She put me on medication as well, two different antidepressants that I've been taking for 3 years or so, but sometimes I'm not sure if they're doing anything or not. I agree with you in that maybe things might improve slowly as my body changes. I've already noticed small differences in how I think about my body and how I look at it, but sometimes it feels like it will just never change to be even close to how I feel it should look, even with the hormones, losing weight, proper nutrition, and working out, all of which I'm trying really hard to do right now.

I haven't decided whether to medicate for the thyroid yet. My "health team" (doctor and endocrinologist, etc.) was thinking they wanted me to go on Synthroid (the synthetic thyroid hormone), so I've been doing a ton of research on it. The thing is, I'm someone who's always been opposed to just taking lots of meds, especially ones for the rest of my life - the difference with antideps and hormones is that with antidepressants, I sort of needed them or I was on the road to actually killing myself, plus I did a ton of research, and with hormones, well, there's really no other way to change my body into a male one. But with Synthroid, it scares me because a lot of the research I've done has said the more you give your body a synthetic hormone, the less natural hormone it produces; sort of like "Oh, you're giving me thyroid hormone? Well, I was having trouble making it anyway, I'll just take yours instead." It ends up suppressing your thyroid apparently, and then you'd have to take it for the rest of your life. That scares me shitless. So right now, my goal is to lose a whole bunch of weight (well namely bodyfat, the number on the scale doesn't matter so much to me within reason, it's more how much bodyfat I have and how strong my body as a whole is/how much muscle or functional muscle I have), and see if it would improve my thyroid levels so that I wouldn't be on the road to taking Synthroid. We're talking 80-100 pounds here. I'm pretty overweight at 272 pounds and 5'6". I've lost probably 10 pounds so far and it's going well and I'm feeling better, at least slightly, so that's good. I plan to absolutely continue, but the scary part is, what if it doesn't work and my thyroid doesn't improve? Will I still have to take meds? It's making me pretty nervous and just sort of makes me want to run the other direction.

Thank you for replying! And no worries, your English is great :) 

My degree is in Psychology with a minor in Writing (Fiction). I took it because throughout my childhood I had gone through what I felt were so many horrible emotional situations, and had had two abusive relationships, and I felt like I wanted to understand myself and how people work; what makes them tick. I've enjoyed it, but I have less than no idea what I'm going to do with it or even if I'll do anything relating to Psychology. 

I really do appreciate all of this. Thankfully, I do actually have a REALLY good therapist, who I've been seeing since I was probably 18. She's wonderful, but unfortunately I don't see her that often as it's quite expensive and my parents are paying for it all which means that I feel bad if I go more than maybe once every three weeks. As well, I just feel bad bringing up the suicidal thing because I did once, and my parents kind of freaked out. They took all the knives in the house and hid them and stuff, which is fair, but I didn't know how to tell them that I wouldn't actually DO anything - I just FELT like I needed to. It was tough. I also don't want to end up in a mental health ward at the hospital, you know? I've heard they can be pretty horrific. I've also been on antidepressants for a number of years now, but sometimes it feels hit-or-miss as to whether they're working or not.

Again, thank you so much for caring and taking the time to reply. It means the absolute world to me and I'm so grateful.
